title: geode-fem site export (Epic #840 Phase 1a)
description: The mesh + swept-field + S-parameter + provenance record a geode-fem solver run is converted into for browser display on klayout-tools.org (issue #849, Phase 1a of Epic #840). `mesh`/`frames` are deliberately shaped to be a strict superset of `site/src/components/field/types.ts`'s `FieldMesh`/`FieldFrame` (an `{mesh, frames}` slice of this document validates directly as that component's `FieldViewerData` prop) so a future consumer (issue #850, not yet built) can feed this file to `FieldViewer` without a translation layer, while `s_parameters`/`radiation_pattern`/`provenance` carry the rest of a solver run's record that a generic mesh+field viewer has no concept of. Produced by `examples/em/patch_antenna/generate.py`; see `docs/design/em-site-export-format.md` for the full design rationale.

schema_version.description: Export format version, independent of any `klt` command's own JSON `schema_version` (docs/json-contract.md) -- this is solver/site-pipeline output, not a `klt` command response.

benchmark.description: Which geode-fem benchmark family this export was generated from, e.g. `"patch_antenna"`.

mesh.description: A 3D surface mesh -- same shape as `FieldMesh` (site/src/components/field/types.ts). For a volumetric FEM solve this is a derived planar cross-section (marching-tetrahedra slice), never the raw tetrahedral volume mesh directly (a tet's 4 vertices are not a renderable polygon) -- see `provenance.mesh_reduction` for how a given export's slice/crop was chosen.

vertices.description: One `[x, y, z]` position per vertex, in the solver's native length units (millimeters for geode-fem).

cells.description: Cells (polygons) as 0-based index arrays into `vertices`, in winding order -- triangles for a marching-tetrahedra slice, but not required to be (FieldViewer fan-triangulates n-gons).

frames.description: One or more swept-parameter/frequency field samples, each vertex-aligned 1:1 with `mesh.vertices` -- same shape as an array of `FieldFrame` (site/src/components/field/types.ts), with an added `frequency_hz` FieldViewer itself does not need but a solver-run record does.

label.description: Display label for this sweep point, e.g. `"2.275 GHz"`.

frequency_hz.description: The drive frequency this frame was solved at, in Hz, or `null` for a non-frequency-swept frame.

scalar.description: Per-vertex scalar magnitude (geode-fem: `|E|`, folding real+imaginary components), colormapped directly by FieldViewer. Length must equal `mesh.vertices` length.

vector.description: Per-vertex vector field `[x, y, z]` (geode-fem: the real part of the driven `E` field). Length must equal `mesh.vertices` length.

s_parameters.description: The frequency-swept port response of the solved structure -- the piece a generic mesh+field viewer has no concept of.

ports.description: Port names, e.g. `["p1"]` for a single-port (S11-only) sweep.

reference_impedance_ohm.description: Port reference impedance S11 is computed against.

points.description: One entry per swept frequency point.

bandwidth_10db_hz.description: The -10 dB return-loss bandwidth, or `null` when the sweep's frequency grid does not bracket both -10 dB crossings around the dip (see `bandwidth_10db_note`) -- a documented, honest gap, never a fabricated interpolation past the sweep's own data.

radiation_pattern.description: Optional near-to-far-field (NTFF) radiation-pattern block -- present for benchmarks (like the patch antenna) that exercise it, `null`/omitted otherwise.

cuts.description: Principal-plane cuts (e.g. `e_plane`/`h_plane`), each a `theta_deg` vs. normalized `|E|` pair of equal-length arrays.

provenance.description: Reproducibility record -- mirrors the discipline of `klt`'s own shared `provenance` block (docs/json-contract.md) and `examples/sim/`'s generated-fixture convention: every field in this file traces back to an exact solver build, commit, and geometry, never a silent 'trust me'.

commit.description: Full git commit hash of the geode-fem checkout the solve ran against.

solve_parameters.description: Solver boundary-condition / material parameters (port resistance, absorber, substrate properties, ...) -- fields vary by benchmark family.

mesh_reduction.description: How `mesh`/`frames` were derived from the solver's native volumetric output, when applicable (e.g. a planar slice + crop). `null` when `mesh` is the solver's native mesh unmodified.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp this export file was generated (not when geode-fem was solved -- the two can differ if `--skip-run` re-converted an earlier solver run).
